quantization.title: Static vs Dynamic Quantization
quantization.description: Static quantization requires a representative calibration dataset matched to the inference distribution and yields better compression. Dynamic quantization computes scale/zp at runtime, needs no calibration, but can be slower and less accurate for CNNs.

quantization.title: Per-Channel vs Per-Tensor
quantization.description: Per-channel weights improve accuracy for CNNs but are slower and not supported on all mobile NPUs. Qualcomm NPU requires symmetric per-channel quantization. NVIDIA TensorRT supports per-channel but engine build is slower.

quantization.title: Symmetric vs Asymmetric Quantization
quantization.description: Symmetric quantization (zero point = 0) is easier for accelerators. Asymmetric can improve accuracy but requires hardware support and may fail on some NPUs. QNN/CoreML prefer symmetric.

quantization.title: Calibration Size Sensitivity
quantization.description: Too few samples produce poor statistics; too many slow calibration with diminishing returns. A good starting point is 100-300 samples. Data must match inference distribution.

onnx_export.title: Dynamic Shape Handling
onnx_export.description: ONNX export with fixed batch/sequence dimensions creates inflexible models. Use dynamic_axes to preserve variable dimensions, especially for LLMs.

onnx_export.title: Opset Version Compatibility
onnx_export.description: Higher opsets support more operators but reduce hardware compatibility. QNN and CoreML often require opset 13-17. Default to 14 unless a specific EP demands higher.

onnx_export.title: External Data Format
onnx_export.description: Models with weights >2GB must set use_external_data_format=True, producing a .onnx file plus .onnx_data external tensors. Failure to do so causes ONNX export OOM or invalid model errors.

onnx_export.title: Type Casting Defaults
onnx_export.description: Some frameworks default to float64 for small constants. ONNX Runtime and most EPs prefer float32. Cast constants before export or use OnnxFloatToFloat16 carefully.

pass_ordering.title: Convert Before Quantize
pass_ordering.description: Quantization passes (OnnxQuantization, QNNQuantization) require an ONNX input. Running quantization before OnnxConversion fails with a format mismatch. The canonical chain is Convert -> Optimize -> Quantize -> (Optionally) Float16.

pass_ordering.title: Float16 After Quantization
pass_ordering.description: Running OnnxFloatToFloat16 before INT8 quantization destroys the quantized graph. Apply FP16 after quantization only if you want a pure FP16 model, not a quantized one.

pass_ordering.title: Graph Optimize Before Quantization
pass_ordering.description: Running OnnxModelOptimizer or OrtTransformersOptimization before quantization produces a cleaner graph and often improves quantized accuracy by fusing LayerNorm/Attention patterns.

lora.title: Base Model Frozen
lora.description: LoRA keeps the base model weights frozen and trains only low-rank adapter matrices. This means the base model can be quantized separately, but merging adapters into a quantized base model is non-trivial.

lora.title: Rank Selection
lora.description: Rank 8-16 works for simple tasks; 32-64 for domain adaptation; 128+ for large distribution shifts. Higher rank increases train memory and adapter size.

lora.title: QLoRA + Quantization
lora.description: QLoRA uses a 4-bit base model for training. After training, export the adapter and merge with a non-quantized base before ONNX conversion if you need ONNX. Merging adapters into a 4-bit base is not supported by Olive.

hardware.title: Execution Provider Silent Fallback
hardware.description: If an operator is not implemented for the requested EP, ONNX Runtime may silently fall back to CPUExecutionProvider, causing unexpected latency. Check EP-specific operator support and enable verbose logging.

hardware.title: QNN Operator Whitelist
hardware.description: QNN only supports a subset of ONNX ops. LayerNorm, GELU, and some gather/reshape patterns may need replacement or partitioning. Use QNNPreprocess when available.

studio.title: HfModel for Hugging Face sources
studio.description: Olive 0.13+ rejects hf_config on PyTorchModel. Olive Studio must emit type HfModel with model_path set to the HF id for Hugging Face inputs.

studio.title: Parse & Apply after pull
studio.description: Pull from GitHub and Microsoft Olive shortcuts only fill the JSON editor. Pipeline UI state updates after Parse & Apply.

studio.title: Apply Fix needs applyable config
studio.description: Diagnose may return guidance-only Studio entries (applyable=false). Follow Recommended Fix text; Apply stays disabled until updated_config maps into UI state.

studio.title: Pin mcp package below 2
studio.description: Olive MCP server imports mcp.server.fastmcp, which mcp 2.x removes. Install with mcp<2 in the same venv Olive Studio uses.
